description: Composite of two bright-field TEM micrographs — left in +g and right in −g imaging conditions — of deformed Fe–28% Al, recorded near the [0 0 1] zone axis according to the caption. A black scale bar labelled "0.2µm" is printed in the lower-right corner of the left panel. Both panels show the same dislocation structure: dark dislocation lines on a lighter, mottled matrix, forming a dense irregular network of long straight segments (many in near-screw orientation), curved lines, tangles and small dark debris clusters. A thick black arrow at the lower right of each panel marks the diffraction imaging vector g, stated in the caption to be of type 1 1 0; the two arrows point in opposite senses, denoting the reversal of the imaging vector sign. The right panel carries small "r" labels that are absent from the left panel, marking dislocations that are straight, mutually parallel and distinct from the surrounding tangled network — one near centre-left, a group of three in the upper right, one at mid-right and one at lower-left. The pair demonstrates that these "r" reaction dislocations maintain their straight, parallel character on reversing g. Only the 0.2 µm scale bar is numeric; no g-vector or index text is printed in either panel.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph in +g condition of deformed Fe–28% Al: dark dislocation lines forming a dense tangled network with long straight and curved segments on a lighter mottled matrix; several small dark scale-like features along some lines. Black scale bar labelled '0.2µm' in the bottom-right corner; a thick black arrow at lower right marks the imaging vector g pointing up/right. No 'r' labels are present.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of the same area in −g condition: the same dislocation network, with the imaging arrow now pointing down/right (opposite sense). Several straight, mutually parallel dislocations are labelled 'r' — one near centre-left, a cluster of three in the upper right, one at mid-right and one at lower-left — standing out from the surrounding tangles and curved lines.

observations.observation: The figure is a pair of side-by-side bright-field TEM micrographs in which dislocations appear as dark lines on a lighter, mottled matrix; both panels image the same dislocation structure.
A black scale bar in the lower-right corner of the left panel is labelled '0.2µm'.
Each panel contains a thick black arrow marking the imaging vector g; the left arrow points up/right and the right arrow points down/right, i.e. opposite senses corresponding to +g and −g.

Only the right panel carries 'r' labels, marking straight dislocations that are parallel to one another (one centre-left, three in the upper right, one mid-right, one lower-left); the left panel has no such labels.

The dislocation substructure in both panels consists of long, mostly straight segments alongside curved segments, dense tangles and small dark debris/loop-like clusters, and no precipitates or second-phase particles are resolved.
The caption states the figure is a pair of bright-field micrographs in +g and −g imaging conditions showing straight and parallel reaction dislocations marked 'r' in deformed Fe–28% Al.
The caption states the zone axis is near [0 0 1] and the imaging vector (marked by the arrow) is of type 1 1 0; these labels are not printed inside the micrographs themselves.
The citing text states that many parallel dislocations with identical Burgers vector (marked 'r') are straight and are produced as reactions between segments of glissile 1 1 1-type superdislocations.

The citing text states that such reactions produce a pair of edge dislocations with 1 0 0 Burgers vector sitting in a sessile configuration on a cube plane, e.g. [1 1 1] + [1 1̄ 1] forming a pair of [1 0 0] edge dislocations along [0 1 0] in a (0 0 1) plane.

The citing text states these configurations constitute locks that prevent further room-temperature superdislocation motion, and that these superdislocations do not trail APBI faults (unlike the APBII-trailing perfect B2 superdislocations).
The figure demonstrates that the 'r'-labelled reaction dislocations retain their straight, mutually parallel character when the sign of the imaging vector is reversed between the two panels.

unreadable_items: No g vector, zone axis or diffraction index text is printed inside either micrograph; the imaging vector is indicated only by the arrow symbols and by the caption (type 1 1 0, zone axis near [0 0 1]).
The arrows carry no printed label distinguishing which panel is +g and which is −g; the assignment (left = +g, right = −g) follows the caption's order and the opposite arrow senses.
Caption and citing-sentence text-block identifiers were not supplied with the request; placeholder ids b0001 (caption) and b0002 (citing sentences) are used for evidence linkage.
